questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like documentaries. They are interesting and I learn new things. I like nature documentaries, but sometimes they are sad.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I enjoy watching documentaries. I think they're quite interesting and educational. For example, I watched one about space last week, and it was really fascinating. However, sometimes they can be a bit boring if the topic doesn't interest me.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm a big fan of documentaries, though it depends on my mood. I love the way a good one can shed light on a topic I knew nothing about. Nature and history ones are my go-to, and I usually get hooked and end up watching two or three in a row.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga hujjatli filmlar yoqadi. Ular qiziqarli va men yangi narsalarni o'rganaman. Menga tabiat haqidagi hujjatli filmlar yoqadi, lekin ba'zida ular xafa qiladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men hujjatli filmlarni tomosha qilishni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, ular juda qiziqarli va ma'lumot beruvchi.
Masalan, o'tgan hafta kosmos haqida birini tomosha qildim va u juda hayratlanarli edi.
Biroq, ba'zida mavzu meni qiziqtirmasa, ular biroz zerikarli bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men hujjatli filmlarni tomosha qilishni yoqtiraman, garchi buning uchun kayfiyatim mos bo'lishi kerak. Ularning murakkab masalalarga oydinlik kiritishi yoki meni ilgari o'ylamagan nuqtai nazarlar bilan tanishtirishi menga yoqadi. Men haddan tashqari shov-shuvli hujjatli filmlarning muxlisi bo'lmasam ham, yaxshi o'rganilgan va o'ylab topilgan filmlarni juda foydali deb bilaman. Bu yangi narsani o'rganishning yaxshi usuli, hatto u passiv bo'lsa ham.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you enjoy watching documentaries?
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I absolutely enjoy…" - "Ha, men juda yoqtiraman…"
"I find them incredibly informative…" - "Men ularni juda foydali deb bilaman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I absolutely enjoy watching documentaries. I find them incredibly informative and they often cover topics I wouldn't normally explore on my own.
Nature and history documentaries are my favourites because they broaden my horizons and give me a deeper understanding of the world. I'd say I watch at least one or two a week whenever I get the chance.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men hujjatli filmlarni tomosha qilishdan juda ham zavqlanaman. Men ularni nihoyatda informativ deb bilaman va ular ko'pincha men o'zim mustaqil ravishda o'rganmagan mavzularni qamrab oladi.

Tabiat va tarixga oid hujjatli filmlar mening eng sevimli filmlarim, chunki ular dunyoqarashimni kengaytiradi va menga dunyoni chuqurroq tushunish imkonini beradi. Imkoniyat tug'ilganda, haftasiga kamida bir yoki ikkita tomosha qilaman desam bo'ladi.

questions.prompt: Do you enjoy singing in your free time?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like sing. In the shower.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like singing. I sing when I am happy and I sing in my house. But my family says I am not good.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I enjoy singing in my free time. I'm not very good, but I still like it. I usually sing when I'm alone, for example, when I'm cooking or cleaning. It's a good way to relax, I think.
questions.sampleB2: I do, yeah, though I'm hardly a gifted singer, I have to admit. I tend to belt out my favourite songs when I'm in the shower or doing the washing-up, and honestly, it's a brilliant way to unwind. Nobody's around to judge me, so I just let loose and have a bit of fun.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men qo'shiq aytishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men xursand bo'lganimda qo'shiq aytaman va uyimda qo'shiq aytaman. Lekin oilamdagilar mening yaxshi emasligimni aytishadi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, bo'sh vaqtimda qo'shiq aytishni yoqtiraman. Unchalik yaxshi emasman, lekin baribir menga yoqadi. Odatda yolg'iz bo'lganimda qo'shiq aytaman, masalan, ovqat qilayotganimda yoki tozalamoqda bo'lganimda. Bu dam olishning yaxshi usuli, deb o'ylayman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men qo'shiq kuylashni yoqtiraman, garchi men
albatta havaskorman. Men ovozimni tomoshabinlarga eshittirmagan bo'lardim, lekin bu menga juda terapevtik ta'sir qiladi. Men ko'pincha uy ishlarini qilayotganda musiqa bilan birga kuylayman, yoki ba'zan shunchaki naushniklarni taqib, yakka karaoke sessiyasini o'tkazaman. Bu zo'r stressni yengillashtiruvchi vosita va bu qiziqarli, hatto qo'shnilarim rozi bo'lmasalar ham.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you enjoy singing in your free time?
sentenceStarters: "To be honest, I do enjoy…" - "Rostini aytsam, men yoqtiraman…"
"I think singing is a wonderful way to…" - "Menimcha, qo'shiq aytish ajoyib usul…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I do enjoy singing, although I wouldn't say I'm particularly talented at it. I usually sing along to my favourite songs when I'm driving or doing housework — it really helps me lift my mood.
I think singing is a wonderful way to express emotions, even if you're just doing it for fun rather than performing in front of others.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, qo'shiq aytish menga yoqadi, garchi men unda unchalik iste'dodli emasman desam ham bo'ladi. Odatda mashinada ketayotganimda yoki uy ishlarini qilayotganimda sevimli qo'shiqlarimga qo'shilib kuylayman — bu kayfiyatimni ko'tarishga juda yordam beradi.

Menimcha, qo'shiq aytish — bu his-tuyg'ularni ifoda etishning ajoyib usuli, hatto agar siz buni boshqalar oldida chiqish qilishdan ko'ra, shunchaki o'yin-kulgi uchun qilsangiz ham.

questions.prompt: What do you usually talk about with older people?
questions.sampleA2: I talk to my grandma. We talk about her garden. And what I did at school. It's nice.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I usually talk to older people about their lives. I like to ask them about when they were young. Also, sometimes we talk about the news, but not always. I think it's important to listen to them.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose it usually revolves around the old days, to be honest. My grandparents love reminiscing about how life used to be, and I find it genuinely eye-opening. We also chat about family news and the odd bit of gossip. Now and then we touch on current events, but I try to tread carefully there.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men ob-havo haqida gaplashaman. Va ovqat haqida.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men buvim bilan gaplashaman. Biz uning bog'i haqida gaplashamiz. Va men maktabda nima qilganim haqida. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, men odatda keksa odamlar bilan ularning hayoti haqida gaplashaman. Ulardan yoshligida nimalar bo'lgani haqida so'rashni yaxshi ko'raman. Yana, ba'zida yangiliklar haqida ham gaplashamiz, lekin har doim emas. Menimcha, ularni tinglash muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men keksa odamlar bilan gaplashganimda, suhbat ko'pincha ularning o'tmishdagi tajribalari va hayotga bo'lgan nuqtai nazarlari atrofida bo'ladi. Men, odatda, ularning yillar davomida guvohi bo'lgan o'zgarishlari haqida eshitishga qiziqaman. Biz, shuningdek, joriy voqealar haqida ham gaplashishimiz mumkin, garchi men ularning potentsial sezgirliklarini hisobga olishga harakat qilaman. Men bu suhbatlarni juda qimmatli deb bilaman, chunki ular dunyoga qarash va ularning donoligidan o'rganish uchun noyob imkoniyatni taqdim etadi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What do you usually talk about with older people?
idioms: wisdom comes with age - "yosh bilan donolik keladi"
sentenceStarters: "When I chat with older people, we typically…" - "Katta yoshdagilar bilan gaplashganda, biz odatda…"
"I find it fascinating to hear…" - "Men eshitishni juda qiziq deb bilaman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
When I chat with older people, we typically discuss topics like family, health, and their life experiences. I find it fascinating to hear stories about how things used to be — it gives me a real sense of perspective.
We also sometimes talk about current events, and I enjoy hearing their words of wisdom on various matters. It's always a rewarding conversation.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men keksa odamlar bilan suhbatlashganimda, odatda oila, sog'liq va ularning hayotiy tajribalari kabi mavzularni muhokama qilamiz. Menga narsalar qanday bo'lgani haqidagi hikoyalarni eshitish juda qiziq - bu menga haqiqiy nuqtai nazar beradi.

Biz ba'zan hozirgi voqealar haqida ham gaplashamiz va men ularning turli masalalar bo'yicha hikmatli so'zlarini eshitishdan zavqlanaman. Bu har doim foydali suhbat bo'ladi.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1: I see a man and a girl. They are in a garden. I see a boy and an old man. He is looking at the tablet.
questions.sampleA2: I see a man and a girl in a garden and they are watering plants. The girl is happy. And I see a boy and an old man and the boy is showing him something on a tablet. It is interesting.
questions.sampleB1: In the first picture, I can see a grandfather and a granddaughter. They are outside, maybe in their garden. The grandfather is showing the girl how to water the plants. In the second picture, it looks like a grandson is helping his grandfather to use a tablet. I think it's nice that they are helping each other.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, an elderly man in a straw hat is out in a lush garden with his little granddaughter perched on his lap. He's handing her a watering can and clearly teaching her to look after the plants. In the second one, the tables are turned: a younger man is leaning over an older gentleman, pointing at a tablet and showing him how it works. So while the grandfather passes on gardening know-how, the young man helps out with technology. Both generations are learning from one another, which I find lovely.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men bir erkak va bir qizni ko'ryapman. Ular bog'da. Men bir bola va bir qariya odamni ko'ryapman. U planshetga qarayapti.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men bog'da bir erkak va bir qizni ko'ryapman va ular o'simliklarni sug'orishyapti. Qiz xursand.
Va men bir bola va bir qariyani ko'ryapman va bola unga planshetda nimadir ko'rsatyapti. Bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda men bir bobo va nabirani ko'ryapman. Ular tashqarida, balki o'z bog'larida. Bobo qizga o'simliklarni qanday sug'orishni ko'rsatyapti.
Ikkinchi rasmda esa, nabira bobosiga planshetdan foydalanishga yordam berayotganga o'xshaydi. Menimcha, ular bir-biriga yordam berishlari juda yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda bobosi nabirasiga bog‘dorchilikni o‘rgatayotganga o‘xshaydi. U o‘simliklarni qanday sug‘orishni ko‘rsatyapti, nabirasi esa juda qiziqayotganga o‘xshaydi.
Ikkinchi rasmda esa nabirasi bobosiga planshet yoki boshqa bir texnologiya turidan qanday foydalanishni ko‘rsatayotganga o‘xshaydi. Bu rollarning qanday almashganini ko‘rish juda qiziq; ikkala avlod ham bir-biridan o‘rganmoqda. Bu o‘rganish yoshidan qat’i nazar, umrbod davom etadigan jarayon ekanligini ta’kidlaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: you're never too old to learn - "o'rganish uchun hech qachon kech emas"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see…" - "Birinchi rasmda men ko'ryapman…"
"The contrast is striking…" - "Farq juda yaqqol ko'rinadi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see a grandfather and his granddaughter in a garden. He is gently teaching her how to water plants, and she seems to be eagerly learning this practical skill. It’s a lovely example of passing down knowledge from one generation to the next.
In the second picture, the roles are reversed: a grandson is explaining to his grandfather how to use a tablet. The elderly man looks interested and is paying close attention. The contrast is striking — both images show that regardless of age, people can learn from one another.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda men bobo va uning nabirasini bog'da ko'ryapman. U nabirasiga o'simliklarni qanday sug'orishni ehtiyotkorlik bilan o'rgatyapti va u bu amaliy ko'nikmani ishtiyoq bilan o'rganayotganga o'xshaydi. Bu bir avloddan ikkinchi avlodga bilim o'tkazishning ajoyib namunasi.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa rollar teskari: nabira bobosiga planshetdan qanday foydalanishni tushuntiryapti. Keksa odam qiziqish bilan qarab, diqqat bilan tinglayapti. Farq juda sezilarli – ikkala rasm ham yoshidan qat'i nazar, odamlar bir-biridan o'rganishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of children learning practical skills from older generations?
questions.sampleA1:
Old people good. They teach. Children learn.

Good for help.
questions.sampleA2:
I think it's good. Old people know things.

They can teach kids to cook and fix things. And it's nice for family.
questions.sampleB1:
I think it is good for children to learn from older people.

For example, my grandma knows how to sew. She can teach me.

Also, older people have a lot of experience, so they know what they are doing. It can help children learn faster.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the biggest benefit, I'd say, is that kids pick up hands-on skills you simply can't learn from a textbook, like cooking or basic repairs. On top of that, it brings the family closer together and keeps old traditions alive. There's something special about knowledge being handed down from one generation to the next.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Kattalar yaxshi. Ular o'rgatadi. Bolalar o'rganadi.

Yordam berish uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menimcha, bu yaxshi. Keksa odamlar narsalarni bilishadi.

Ular bolalarga ovqat pishirishni va narsalarni tuzatishni o'rgatishlari mumkin. Va bu oila uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, bolalar katta yoshdagi odamlardan o'rganishi yaxshi.

Masalan, buvim tikishni biladi. U menga o'rgata oladi.

Shuningdek, katta yoshdagi odamlarda tajriba ko'p, shuning uchun ular nima qilayotganini bilishadi. Bu bolalarga tezroq o'rganishga yordam berishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, bolalarning katta avloddan amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rganishining bir qancha afzalliklari bor.

Birinchidan, bu ularga maktablarda o'rgatilmasligi mumkin bo'lgan ko'nikmalarni, masalan, an'anaviy hunarmandchilik yoki uy sharoitida ta'mirlash kabi ko'nikmalarni o'rganishga imkon beradi. Bu ko'nikmalar hayotda juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin.

Ikkinchidan, bu oila a'zolari o'rtasida yanada kuchli aloqani mustahkamlaydi va madaniy merosni saqlashga yordam beradi. Katta yoshdagi odamlar ko'nikmalari bilan birga hikoyalar va urf-odatlarni baham ko'rishlari mumkin.

Va nihoyat, bu bolalarga boshqacha o'rganish tajribasini taqdim etadi, bu shunchaki nazariyaga emas, balki real dunyo bilimi va tajribasiga asoslangan.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of children learning practical skills from older generations?
idioms: experience is the best teacher - "tajriba — eng yaxshi o'qituvchi"
sentenceStarters: "There are numerous benefits when…" - "…ning ko'plab foydali tomonlari bor…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are numerous benefits when children learn practical skills from older generations. First of all, skills like cooking, gardening, or basic repairs are extremely useful in everyday life and help children become more self-sufficient.
Beyond the practical aspect, this kind of learning strengthens family bonds and creates a sense of connection between generations. Older people often have a wealth of experience that simply cannot be found in textbooks or online tutorials.
Furthermore, this process helps preserve cultural traditions and keeps valuable knowledge alive. As the saying goes, "experience is the best teacher", and passing these skills down ensures they won't be lost over time.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bolalar katta avloddan amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rganganlarida ko'plab foydali jihatlar mavjud. Avvalo, ovqat pishirish, bog'dorchilik yoki oddiy ta'mirlash kabi ko'nikmalar kundalik hayotda juda foydali bo'lib, bolalarning o'ziga yetarli bo'lishiga yordam beradi.
Amaliy jihatdan tashqari, bunday o'rganish oilaviy rishtalarni mustahkamlaydi va avlodlar o'rtasida aloqa hissini yaratadi. Katta yoshdagi odamlarda shunchaki darsliklarda yoki onlayn qo'llanmalarda topib bo'lmaydigan katta tajriba mavjud.
Bundan tashqari, bu jarayon madaniy an'analarni saqlashga yordam beradi va qimmatli bilimlarni tirik saqlaydi. Aytishlaricha, "tajriba eng yaxshi o'qituvchi", va bu ko'nikmalarni o'rgatish ularning vaqt o'tishi bilan yo'qolmasligini ta'minlaydi.

questions.prompt: Why is it important for younger people to help the elderly with modern technology?
questions.sampleA1: I think it is good. They can learn phone. I help grandma.
questions.sampleA2: It is important because old people don't know computers. And I know computers. So I can help them. It's nice.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's important for young people to help older people with technology. They didn't grow up with it, so it's hard for them. If we help them, they can use the internet and talk to their families. Also, it's a good thing to do.
questions.sampleB2: The thing is, so much of daily life has moved online these days, from banking to booking a doctor's appointment. If we don't lend a hand, older people can easily get left behind and feel cut off. By showing them the ropes, we help them stay in touch with loved ones and keep their independence.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menimcha, bu yaxshi. Ular telefonni o'rganishlari mumkin. Men buvimga yordam beraman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Bu muhim, chunki keksa odamlar kompyuterni bilishmaydi. Men esa kompyuterni bilaman. Shuning uchun men ularga yordam bera olaman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, yoshlar keksalarga texnologiya bilan yordam berishi muhim. Ular texnologiya bilan
katta bo'lishmagan, shuning uchun ularga qiyin. Agar biz ularga yordam bersak, ular internetdan foydalanishlari va oilalari bilan gaplashishlari mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu yaxshi ish.
questions.uzSampleB2: Yosh avlodning keksalarga zamonaviy texnologiyalar bilan yordam berishi juda muhim, chunki texnologiya hozirda kundalik hayotga shunchalik singib ketgan. Ko'p keksa odamlar moslashishda qiynalishadi va yordamsiz ular ajralib qolish va muhim xizmatlardan foydalana olmaslik xavfi ostida qoladilar. Ularga smartfonlar va internet kabi narsalardan qanday foydalanishni o'rgatish orqali biz ularning mustaqilligini saqlab qolish va o'z jamoalari bilan aloqada bo'lish imkoniyatini beramiz. Bundan tashqari, bu avlodlararo tushunishni rivojlantiradi va ijtimoiy aloqalarni mustahkamlaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why is it important for younger people to help the elderly with modern technology?
sentenceStarters: "I think it's extremely important for…" - "Menimcha, …uchun juda muhim…"
"In today's world, so many…" - "Bugungi dunyoda juda ko'p…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I think it's extremely important for younger people to help the elderly navigate modern technology. In today's world, so many essential services — from banking to healthcare appointments — have moved online, and without digital literacy, older people risk being left behind.
By helping them learn to use smartphones, apps, or video calls, we enable them to stay connected with family and friends, which is vital for their mental well-being. It also shows mutual respect — just as they taught us life skills, we can return the favour by sharing our tech knowledge.
As they say, "one good turn deserves another". Ultimately, bridging the digital divide helps create a more inclusive society for everyone.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, yoshlarning keksalarga zamonaviy texnologiyalarni o'zlashtirishda yordam berishi juda muhim. Bugungi kunda ko'plab muhim xizmatlar - bankdan tortib sog'liqni saqlash uchrashuvlarigacha - onlaynga ko'chdi va raqamli savodxonliksiz keksa odamlar ortda qolib ketish xavfi ostida.

Ularga smartfonlar, ilovalar yoki video qo'ng'iroqlardan foydalanishni o'rgatish orqali biz ularga oilasi va do'stlari bilan aloqada bo'lish imkonini beramiz, bu ularning ruhiy farovonligi uchun juda muhimdir. Bu, shuningdek, o'zaro hurmatni ko'rsatadi - xuddi ular bizga hayotiy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatganidek, biz ham o'z texnologiya bilimlarimizni baham ko'rish orqali ularga yaxshilik qila olamiz.

Aytishlaricha, "bir yaxshilikka ming yaxshilik". Oxir oqibat, raqamli tafovutni bartaraf etish har bir kishi uchun yanada inklyuziv jamiyat yaratishga yordam beradi.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you borrowed something useful from a friend.
questions.sampleA1: I borrow book from friend. It is good. I read it. Thank you.
questions.sampleA2: I borrowed a book from my friend. It was a cookbook. I wanted to make a cake, and I needed a recipe. The book helped me, and the cake was good!
questions.sampleB1: Once, I borrowed a camera from my friend. I wanted to go on a trip, and I didn't have a good camera. I think it was very helpful because I could take nice photos. Also, my friend was happy to help me. However, I was very careful with it, because I didn't want to break it.
questions.sampleB2: I'd like to tell you about the time I borrowed a friend's DSLR camera for a weekend trip to the mountains. I'd been dying to get into photography for ages, but I couldn't really justify splashing out on such an expensive bit of kit for something I'd only just taken up. So when my friend Alex offered to lend me his, I jumped at the chance. To be honest, borrowing that camera made a world of difference. My phone camera is fine for snapshots, but it just can't capture the sweeping landscapes and the golden light at sunrise the way a proper camera can. Alex spent a good hour walking me through the settings before I set off, which really helped me get to grips with the basics. By the end of the trip, I'd taken hundreds of shots, and a handful of them turned out genuinely stunning — a couple are still framed on my wall. Without his generosity, I would have missed out on all of that and probably given up on the hobby altogether. As for why sharing resources matters in a community, I honestly think it's what holds people together. Not everyone can afford to buy everything they need, so lending and borrowing levels the playing field and stops money from being a barrier. On top of that, it builds trust and brings neighbours closer, because you're relying on one another and giving back in return. At the end of the day, a community that shares is a much stronger and warmer place to live.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men do'stimdan kitob oldim. U yaxshi edi. Men uni o'qidim. Rahmat.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'stimdan kitob oldim. Bu pazandalik kitobi edi. Men tort tayyorlamoqchi edim va menga retsept kerak edi. Kitob menga yordam berdi va tort mazali chiqdi!
questions.uzSampleB1:
Bir marta, men do'stimdan kamera olib turdim. Men sayohatga bormoqchi edim, va menda yaxshi kamera yo'q edi. O'ylashimcha, bu juda foydali bo'ldi, chunki men chiroyli suratlar olishim mumkin edi. Shuningdek, do'stim menga yordam berganidan xursand edi.
Biroq, men u bilan juda ehtiyot bo'ldim, chunki uni sindirib qo'yishni xohlamadim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Esimda, bir marta qo'shnimdan bosimli yuvish mashinasini olganman. Mening ayvonim kir va mox bilan qoplangan edi va men barbekyu qilishni rejalashtirayotgan edim. Uni ijaraga olish juda qiyin bo'lib tuyuldi, shuning uchun men undan mashinasini olsam bo'ladimi deb so'radim. U juda foydali edi; menga ko'p vaqt va kuchni tejadi va ayvon yangidek ko'rinib qoldi. Bundan tashqari, bu keyinroq suhbatlashib, pivo ichganimiz sababli, jamiyat tuyg'usini ham shakllantirdi.

vocabulary.title: Q7 - Describe a time you borrowed something useful from a friend
idioms: a friend in need is a friend indeed - "boshingga kulfat tushganda do'st bilinadi"
sentenceStarters: "I'd like to talk about a time when…" - "Men bir paytni aytib bermoqchiman…"
"As for why sharing resources is…" - "Resurslarni bo'lishishning sababi…"

bulletPoints: Describe a time you borrowed something useful from a friend.
How did borrowing this item help you?
Why is sharing resources important in a community?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I borrowed something useful:
I'd like to talk about a time when I borrowed a laptop from my close friend during my final exams. My own computer had unexpectedly broken down just a few days before my deadline, and I was in a real state of panic.
How borrowing this item helped me:
Borrowing this laptop was incredibly helpful because it allowed me to finish my research papers and submit all my assignments on time. Without it, I would have had to rely on the university library, which was always packed with students at that time of year. My friend's generous gesture truly saved me from a very stressful situation, and I made sure to return the favour later by helping them with their project.
Why sharing resources is important:
As for why sharing resources is important in a community, I believe it builds trust and strengthens relationships between people. When we share what we have, we create a support network that benefits everyone. Not everyone can afford to buy everything they need, so lending and borrowing levels the playing field.

Foydali narsa qarzga olgan vaqtim:
Men imtihonlar paytida yaqin do'stimdan noutbuk qarzga olganim haqida gapirmoqchiman. Mening kompyuterim topshirish muddatimdan bir necha kun oldin kutilmaganda buzilib qoldi va men juda vahimada edim.
Bu narsani qarzga olish menga qanday yordam berdi:
Bu noutbukni qarzga olish juda foydali bo'ldi, chunki u menga tadqiqot ishlarimni tugatishga va barcha topshiriqlarimni o'z vaqtida topshirishga imkon berdi. Bo'lmasa, men universitet kutubxonasiga tayanishim kerak bo'lar edi, u yilning o'sha paytida doimo talabalar bilan gavjum bo'lardi. Do'stimning saxiy imo-ishorasi meni juda stressli vaziyatdan qutqardi va men ularga loyihalarida yordam berib, keyinroq yaxshiligini qaytarishga harakat qildim.
Nima uchun resurslarni baham ko'rish muhim:
Nima uchun jamiyatda resurslarni baham ko'rish muhimligi haqida gapiradigan bo'lsak, menimcha, bu odamlar o'rtasida ishonchni mustahkamlaydi va munosabatlarni kuchaytiradi. Bizda bor narsalarni baham ko'rsak, hamma uchun foydali bo'lgan qo'llab-quvvatlash tarmog'ini yaratamiz. Hamma ham o'ziga kerak bo'lgan hamma narsani sotib olishga qurbi yetmaydi, shuning uchun qarz berish va qarz olish imkoniyatlarni tenglashtiradi.

questions.prompt: Professional athletes are paid too much money.
questions.sampleA1: Yes. Money too much. Football player. I like football.
questions.sampleA2: I think yes, they get too much money. They play games, and it's fun, but doctors are more important. Doctors help people who are sick, and they don't get so much money. But athletes are famous.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think professional athletes probably get paid too much, to be honest. I mean, they're good at sports, but is it really worth millions of dollars? Teachers and nurses are more important, and they don't earn nearly as much. However, I suppose the athletes do bring in a lot of money for the teams. So, it's complicated.
questions.sampleB2: This is a real hot-button issue, and I can genuinely see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, plenty of people argue that top athletes are wildly overpaid. When you compare a footballer earning millions a week to a nurse or a teacher scraping by on a modest salary, the gap does seem hard to justify. Critics also point out that all that money could be put to far better use — funding public sports facilities or local charities, for instance. And there's the knock-on effect on fans, since sky-high wages tend to push up ticket prices, gradually pricing ordinary supporters out of the stadium. On the other hand, the opposing camp makes a fair point too. Athletes have remarkably short careers, often just a decade or so, and they're constantly putting their bodies on the line, risking injuries that can haunt them for life. What's more, the very best bring in enormous revenue for their clubs, sponsors and host cities, so in a way they're simply earning their keep. The talent and dedication it takes to reach the top are incredibly rare, and the market rewards that accordingly. Personally, I reckon the truth lies somewhere in between. I don't begrudge athletes a good living — they've worked their socks off to get there — but the sheer scale of some salaries does strike me as excessive when so many essential workers are struggling. At the end of the day, it says a lot about what our society chooses to value, and I think that balance is well worth rethinking.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly controversial topic that sparks strong opinions on both sides. Those who believe professional athletes are overpaid argue that their salaries are disproportionate to their actual contribution to society, especially when compared to essential workers like doctors or teachers who earn a fraction of that amount. They also point out that the massive sums of money could be better allocated to public sports facilities or local charities. Furthermore, inflated player wages drive up ticket prices, making live sports increasingly unaffordable for ordinary fans.
However, those on the opposing side make some compelling arguments too. Athletes typically have very short careers — often just ten to fifteen years — and they risk severe physical injuries that can affect them for the rest of their lives. Additionally, they generate massive revenue for their teams, sponsors, and host cities through entertainment and tourism.
Personally, I think the truth lies somewhere in the middle. As the saying goes, "the labourer is worthy of his hire", but perhaps there should be more balance in how society rewards different professions.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu juda bahsli mavzu bo'lib, har ikki tomonda ham kuchli fikrlarni uyg'otadi. Professional sportchilarga haddan tashqari ko'p pul to'lanadi, deb hisoblaydiganlar ularning maoshlari jamiyatga qo'shgan hissalariga nomutanosib ekanligini ta'kidlaydilar, ayniqsa, shifokorlar yoki o'qituvchilar kabi muhim ishchilar bilan solishtirganda, ular bu miqdorning bir qismini oladilar. Ular, shuningdek, katta miqdordagi pullarni jamoat sport inshootlariga yoki mahalliy xayriya tashkilotlariga yaxshiroq yo'naltirish mumkinligini ta'kidlaydilar. Bundan tashqari, o'yinchilarning oshirilgan maoshlari chiptalar narxini oshiradi va jonli sportni oddiy muxlislar uchun tobora qimmatlashtiradi.

Biroq, qarama-qarshi tomonda bo'lganlar ham ba'zi bir ishonarli dalillarni keltiradilar. Sportchilar odatda juda qisqa faoliyatga ega - ko'pincha atigi o'n-o'n besh yil - va ular hayotining qolgan qismiga ta'sir qilishi mumkin bo'lgan jiddiy jismoniy jarohatlar xavfini tug'diradi. Bundan tashqari, ular ko'ngilochar va turizm orqali o'z jamoalari, homiylari va mezbon shaharlari uchun katta daromad olib keladilar.

Shaxsan men, haqiqat o'rtada deb o'ylayman. Aytganlaridek, "ishchi o'z haqiga loyiq", lekin jamiyat turli kasblarni qanday taqdirlashida ko'proq muvozanat bo'lishi kerak.
